steps.tx: **Mucormycosis** is an **angioinvasive** mould infection by **Mucorales**, most often **Rhizopus**. Fungi invade vessels, clot them and kill tissue within days. Rhino-cerebral disease still kills despite treatment. **Diabetic ketoacidosis** and **neutropenia** cause most cases. **Black necrotic eschar** is the classic warning sign.
steps.say: Mucormycosis is an infection by a group of moulds called Mucorales, with Rhizopus the commonest. These fungi were reported to invade vessel walls, clot them and kill tissue within days. Disease around the nose and brain is associated with death in more than four in ten despite treatment. Diabetic ketoacidosis and low neutrophils cause most cases, and a black dead patch of skin or palate is the classic warning.

steps.tx: **Uncontrolled diabetes** with **ketoacidosis** is the top risk in India; **neutropenia** tops elsewhere with transplant and blood cancers. **Iron overload** with **deferoxamine** feeds the fungus. **Voriconazole prophylaxis** selects breakthrough mucor. **Trauma, burns and contaminated dressings** seed skin disease. **Steroids with COVID** triggered the recent epidemic wave.
steps.say: Uncontrolled diabetes with ketoacidosis is the leading risk in India, while low neutrophils lead elsewhere, with transplant and blood cancers close behind. Iron overload treated with deferoxamine feeds the fungus, and voriconazole prevention paradoxically selects for mucor. Wounds, burns and dirty dressings seed skin disease, and steroids given for covid triggered the recent epidemic.

steps.tx: **Broad nonseptate hyphae** with **right angle branching** mark Mucorales on smear. **Angioinvasion** clots vessels so tissue dies black and drugs reach poorly. **Acid with free iron** in ketoacidosis feeds growth. **Galactomannan with beta-D-glucan stay negative**, unlike aspergillus. **Ribbon-like hyphae** on histopathology with culture proves it; blood cultures almost never grow.
steps.say: On a smear, Mucorales showed broad hyphae without septa branching at right angles. They demonstrated invasion of vessel walls with clotting, so the tissue turns black and drugs reach the site poorly. Acid blood with free iron in ketoacidosis was reported to feed their growth. Unlike aspergillus, the blood biomarkers galactomannan and beta-D-glucan stayed negative in case series. Ribbon-like hyphae on biopsy with culture confirmed the diagnosis, since blood cultures almost never grew.

steps.tx: **Facial pain with bloody discharge** opens rhino-orbital disease. **Black eschar** on palate or turbinate seals suspicion. **Eye swelling with ophthalmoplegia** means orbital spread; **cavernous sinus** follows fast. **CT with MRI** maps sinuses, orbit and brain. **Nasal endoscopy with biopsy** at once; never wait for cultures in suspected cases.
steps.say: Facial pain with bloody nasal discharge marked the opening of rhino-orbital disease. A black dead patch on the palate or turbinate sealed the suspicion. A swollen eye that stopped moving indicated orbital involvement, with the cavernous sinus following fast. C T with M R I mapped the sinuses, orbit and brain. Nasal endoscopy with biopsy was advised at once, without waiting for cultures in suspected cases.

steps.tx: **Pulmonary mucor** strikes neutropenia with **fever unresponsive** to antibacterials. **Reverse halo sign** on CT favours mucor over aspergillus. **Cutaneous disease** follows trauma with blackening wounds. **Gut disease** bleeds in malnutrition. **Disseminated infection** seeds brain and kills most; blood spread marks late disease.
steps.say: Lung mucor was reported in patients with low neutrophils as fever ignoring antibacterials. On C T, a reverse halo sign favoured mucor over aspergillus. Skin disease followed wounds that turned black. Gut disease presented with bleeding in malnourished patients. Once the fungus spread in blood to the brain, most patients died, so dissemination marked late disease.

steps.tx: **KOH mount with histopathology** is the first test; **broad aseptate hyphae** decide within hours. **Culture** names species but stays negative often. **CT shows reverse halo** in lung; **MRI tracks** orbit and brain spread. **Biomarkers stay negative**, so normal galactomannan never excludes. **Biopsy with debridement tissue** doubles as diagnosis with treatment.
steps.say: The first test is a K O H mount with histopathology, where broad hyphae without septa decided the matter within hours. Culture named the species but often stayed negative. C T showed the reverse halo in the lung, while M R I tracked spread into the orbit and brain. Biomarkers stayed negative, so a normal galactomannan never excluded mucor. Tissue taken during surgical cleaning doubled as diagnosis and treatment.

nodes.label: KOH smear plus CT or MRI

steps.tx: **Liposomal amphotericin B 5 to 10 mg/kg daily** leads urgently; delay kills. **Correct ketoacidosis**, recover neutrophils and **stop deferoxamine with voriconazole** at once. **Surgical consult** comes early, not after drugs fail. **Posaconazole with isavuconazole** never replaces amphotericin upfront. **Treat through the whole** risk period; stopping early relapses.
steps.say: Liposomal amphotericin B was started at five to ten milligrams per kilo every day without delay, because delay killed. The ketoacidosis was corrected, neutrophils recovered, and deferoxamine with voriconazole stopped at once. Surgeons were called early, not after drugs failed. Posaconazole with isavuconazole never replaced amphotericin as the first drug. Treatment continued through the whole risk period, since stopping early brought relapse.

steps.tx: **Wide surgical debridement** decides survival in rhino-orbital disease; **orbital exenteration** when vision is lost with spread. **Step down to posaconazole or isavuconazole** after control for months. **Voriconazole never works** against Mucorales. **Diabetes control with secondary prophylaxis** runs through immunosuppression. **Follow with endoscopy with imaging** till healed.
steps.say: Wide surgical cleaning decided survival in disease around the nose and eye, including removing the eye contents when vision was lost and infection spread. After control, treatment stepped down to posaconazole or isavuconazole tablets for months. Voriconazole never worked against Mucorales. Diabetes stayed controlled with preventive antifungals through the immunosuppressed period. Follow-up used endoscopy with imaging till healing.

steps.tx: **Rhino-cerebral disease** carries the worst odds once **brain or cavernous sinus** is hit. **Pulmonary disease** in persistent neutropenia kills most. **Cutaneous disease** confined to skin cures with surgery. **Relapse clusters** where risk persists; **secondary prophylaxis** with azoles bridges transplant. **Early combined therapy** is the only survival lever.
steps.say: Disease around the nose and brain carried the worst odds once the brain or cavernous sinus was hit. Lung disease with persistent low neutrophils was associated with death in most patients. Skin disease confined to the skin was cured with surgery alone. Relapse clustered where the risk persisted, so preventive azoles bridged the transplant period. Early combined medical and surgical therapy remained the only lever that improved survival.

steps.tx: **Exam traps:** voriconazole given for suspected aspergillus feeds mucor instead. **Waiting for culture** before surgery kills; smear suffices. **Steroids continued** through infection worsen spread. **Normal biomarkers** mislead away from mould. **Stopping amphotericin** at first improvement relapses; complete the full course.
steps.say: For the exam, revise these traps as tabulated. Voriconazole given for suspected aspergillus fed mucor instead. Waiting for culture before surgery killed, while a smear sufficed. Continuing steroids through the infection worsened spread. Normal biomarkers misled doctors away from mould. Stopping amphotericin at the first improvement brought relapse, so the full course was completed.

steps.tx: **High yield for the exam:** DKA with **black eschar** marks rhino-cerebral mucor. **Reverse halo** marks lung disease. **Right angle aseptate hyphae** prove it; biomarkers stay negative. **Liposomal amphotericin B 5 to 10 mg/kg** leads; **debridement** decides survival. **Voriconazole never** works; **posaconazole** steps down.
steps.say: For the exam, revise these high-yield facts as tabulated. A black dead patch in diabetic ketoacidosis is associated with disease around the nose and brain. A reverse halo on C T indicates lung disease. Right-angle hyphae without septa confirm it, while biomarkers stay negative. Liposomal amphotericin B at five to ten milligrams per kilo leads treatment, and surgical cleaning decides survival. Voriconazole never works, and posaconazole is the step-down drug.
